model_annotations.Bulgarian: The image displays a section of a research paper titled “TaskSpec: A Data-Driven Automated Task Partitioning Method for Speculative Decoding in LLMs,” presented at ICPP 2025 in San Diego, CA. The visible text outlines the paper’s contributions, including the proposal of TaskSpec, a system that automates task-oriented clustering of draft model outputs to improve speculative decoding efficiency. It describes how TaskSpec constructs a heterogeneous draft model dataset, trains a prompt classifier for task-specific draft models, and dynamically selects the most suitable draft model for each user request. The paper also mentions experimental results showing speedups over vanilla speculative decoding on LLaMA-2-13B and LLaMA-M models. Below the main text, a caption reads “tokens in the domains of chemistry (4) and mathematics (9)”, indicating that the paper discusses token distribution patterns across these domains, with chemistry having four tokens and mathematics having nine. The text further references Figure 2, which is not visible in the image, as an example of context-dependent token associations in chemistry-related contexts. The layout includes author names at the top right and publication details at the top left.
model_annotations.English: The image displays a scientific paper titled “TaskSpec: An Automated Speculative Decoding System for Downstream Tasks,” presented at ICPP 2025 in San Diego, CA. The paper introduces TaskSpec, a speculative decoding approach tailored to downstream tasks in large language models (LLMs). It aims to balance drafting accuracy and inference efficiency by first collecting user-input pairs, clustering them into task-specific datasets, and training specialized draft models for each cluster. The system further employs a lightweight prompt classifier to dynamically select the most suitable draft model for each user request. Experimental results show TaskSpec achieves speedups of 1.5x, 2.6x, and 1.8x over vanilla speculative decoding on four downstream tasks. The paper also includes a figure illustrating token distributions in chemistry and mathematics domains, highlighting context-dependent token co-occurrence patterns. The text is structured with an abstract, introduction, overview, and sections detailing the proposed method, experimental results, and related work.
model_annotations.German: Das Kreisdiagramm illustriert die Verteilung von Tokens in zwei Domänen: Chemie (C) und Mathematik (M), wobei die Gesamtanzahl der dargestellten Segmente zwei beträgt. Das erste Segment, das die Chemie darstellt, ist in einem dunklen Blauton gehalten und nimmt etwa 60 Prozent der Fläche ein. Das zweite Segment, das die Mathematik repräsentiert, ist in einem dunklen Rottönen dargestellt und macht etwa 40 Prozent aus. Das Diagramm enthält keine Legende oder Prozentangaben innerhalb der Segmente, sondern die Kategorien sind direkt durch die Beschriftungen „C“ und „M“ identifiziert. Die Segmente sind im Uhrzeigersinn angeordnet, wobei das chemische Segment links oben und das mathematische Segment rechts unten positioniert ist, was eine visuelle Abfolge nach absteigender Größe suggeriert.
